takeaway: The femoral sheath has three compartments: lateral for the femoral artery, intermediate for the femoral vein and medial (the femoral canal) for lymphatics.

question.text: On ultrasound for a femoral central line, several fascial planes are seen. In which compartment of the femoral sheath does the femoral vein lie?

lines.text: On ultrasound, the femoral sheath is a fascial tube in the femoral triangle.
It continues down from the transversalis fascia of the abdominal wall.
It has only three compartments: lateral, intermediate and medial.
The femoral artery lies in the lateral compartment.
The femoral vein sits in the intermediate compartment, right where the catheter goes.
The medial compartment, the femoral canal, holds the lymphatics.
The femoral nerve stays outside the sheath.
So the vein lies in the intermediate compartment.
